 now 07.34 EST 3 min: Now Bernd Leno gets on the ball, lumping it long towards Rodrigo Muniz. The ball’s played wide to Kenny Tete, whose cross from the right is plucked from the air by Donnarumma.
 Share 50s ago 07.33 EST 2 min: A goalkeeper under a little bit of pressure after some recent ricks, Gianluigi Donnarumma gets a couple of early touches, fielding two back-passes with a minimum of fuss.
 Share 2m ago 07.31 EST Manchester CIty v Fulham is go ...
 1 min: Fulham get the ball rolling, their players wearing red shirts, shorts and socks. Manchester City’s are in their usual home colours.
 Share 7m ago 07.26 EST Not long now: Led by referee Tom Bramall and his team of match officials, both sets of players click-clack out on to the Etihad Stadium pitchon a crisp November afternoon in Manchester. They receive a guard of honour from an array of “Once A Blue” Manchester City legends including Mick McCarthy, Peter Barnes, Paul Lake and Davids White and Brightwell.
 Share 29m ago 07.05 EST Enzo Maresca: The Manchester City boss was asked about the balance – or lack thereof – between attack and defence in his side during his audience with the press yesterday. “The same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same that lost three games in a row,” he said. “It’s football. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way, creating chances, but trying to create a balance when we defend. Sometimes we need more balance and different kind of players on the pitch. We are going to find solutions for a more balanced defensive back line and midfield.
 “I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we were winning games. I’m not thinking we did everything wrong when we lost games. There are things we need to do better and no doubt we will do better. We are conceding too many goals. Most of them are avoidable. So we need to avoid mistakes and try to deal with it [better] when it happens.”
 View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City side come into today’s match on the back of three consecutive defeats. Photograph: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images Share 29m ago 07.04 EST Manchester City: Will Unwin is at the Etihad Stadium for the Guardian and has filed this scene-setter from his place in the press box. “Without going over the top, it feels like a big day for Enzo Maresca,” he says. “After three Premier League defeats in a row, the Italian has to find improvement in his team. To do so, a change in midfield sees Ayyoub Bouaddi brought in to bring additional calmness alongside the all-action Elliot Anderson. With all the uncertainty swirling around this half of Manchester, getting matters on the pitch back on track is imperative. A statement win to prove there is full focus among the squad would be ideal but any will do against Fulham.”
 Share 32m ago 07.02 EST Alvaro Arbeloa: “I have watched all Manchester City games and the last three games that they lost I woudn’t say they were the worst team,” said Fulham’s head coach in yesterday’s press conference. “They have the chances. You can see the quality of the players, how they want to play. They are very, very aggressive when they lose the ball, so for me they are performing really, really well.
 “This is the Premier League , so you can feel how difficult every game is, but they won the first seven games, it was amazing. For me, they’re still one of the best teams in the world.”
 Asked about speculation linking Fulham defender Calvin Bassey with a move to Manchester United, Alvaro stressed the Nigerian international’s importance to the Cottagers. “He’s very, very important,” he said. “He is one of my captains. From the first days when I arrived I saw how good he is. I think he is one of the best centre backs in the world, so it’s normal if there are so many teams that wants Calvin, that for me is normal.
 “I’m not worried about that because I am really happy with Calvin. I think Calvin is really happy here. He is so important for us. He is one of our leaders.”
 View image in fullscreen Alvaro Arbeloa doesn’t think Manchester City are in as much trouble as their recent Premier League results suggest. Photograph: Jon Super/Reuters Share 1h ago 06.32 EST Those teams: Enzo Maresca makes three changes to the City team that started against Nottingham Forest last time out, with Nico O’Reilly, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Phil Foden coming into his side. Josko Gvardiol, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki drop to the bench. Abdukodir Khusanov and Marc Guehi have both been selected despite missing out on international duty with Uzbekistan and England resepectively through injury.
 There are also three changes to the Fulham side that lined up against Newcastle before the international break. Kenny Tete, Ryan Sessegnon and Rodrigo Muniz have been selected today, with Timothy Castagne, Antonee Robinson and Gonzalo Garcia making way.

 Share 1h ago 06.25 EST Early team news
 Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo remains sidelined with the knee injury he suffered against Ipswich in October, while defenders Marc Guehi and Abdukodir Khushanov have been rated doubtful for today’s game.
 Speaking at his press conference yesterday, Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa confirmed that reserve goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will be out for the season after rupturing his achillles tendon in a practice match played against West Ham behind closed doors during the international break.
 Midfielder Tom Cairney is struggling with a knee injury but could feature in today’s squad, while Emile Smith-Rowe is unlikely to be in the matchday squad as he has a hip injury.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo misses out on today’s match as he continues his recovery from a knee injury. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Share 1h ago 06.25 EST Premier League: Manchester City v Fulham
 Following the second international break of the season, the Premier League resumes at the Etihad Stadium, with Manchester City hoping to halt a run of three consecutive defeats in the top flight. The most recent came against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, where Liam Delap scored two quite extraordinary goals against the club where he learnt his trade.
 Fulham are unbeaten in four matches and came from behind to draw with Newcastle at Craven Cottage last time out. Rather astonishingly, they haven’t beaten Manchester City since 2009 and have lost 20 consecutive games against today’s hosts in an extraordinary run of defeats against the same opponents dating back to 2012. Kick-off at the Etihad Stadium is at 12.30pm (GMT) but we’ll have team news and buildup in the meantime.
